definition: Augmented Analytics is an approach of data analytics that employs the use of machine learning and natural language processing to automate analysis processes normally done by a specialist or data scientist.
details: The term was introduced in 2017 by Rita Sallam, Cindi Howson, and Carlie Idoine in a Gartner research paper. Augmented analytics is based on business intelligence and analytics. In the graph extraction step, data from different sources are investigated.

explainer.lead: Augmented analytics uses machine learning and natural language processing to automate parts of data analysis usually handled by specialists. Building on business intelligence and analytics, it aims to reduce the manual work involved in examining data.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a helper that can spot patterns in numbers and read written comments. It helps a business examine information from different places and do some of the work a data expert would normally do, while people still check and understand the findings.
tiers.practitioner: Apply it within business intelligence and analytics workflows where machine learning and natural language processing can automate analysis normally performed by a specialist or data scientist. During graph extraction, investigate data from different sources; do not assume automation removes the need to check input quality and interpret results carefully.
tiers.paperLevel: Augmented analytics = the use of machine learning and natural language processing to automate analysis processes in business intelligence and analytics that are normally performed by specialists or data scientists. The term was introduced in 2017 by Rita Sallam, Cindi Howson, and Carlie Idoine in a Gartner research paper. Its graph extraction step involves investigating data from different sources.

explainer.example: A business intelligence team combines sales records and customer comments from separate systems. Machine learning examines the sales patterns while natural language processing handles the comments, and the automated analysis highlights a region where falling sales coincide with repeated complaints about late deliveries.

usedIn.name: Business intelligence
usedIn.detail: Provides one of the foundations on which augmented analytics is built.

usedIn.name: Data analytics
usedIn.detail: Uses machine learning and natural language processing to automate analysis processes.

usedIn.name: Data science
usedIn.detail: Automates analytical work that would normally be done by a data scientist or specialist.

explainer.intuition: The idea is to add learning and language capabilities to established analytics work. This lets software handle analysis steps that would otherwise require a specialist.
howItWorks: Bring in data from different sources.
Investigate the data during graph extraction.
Apply machine learning and natural language processing.
Automate analysis processes normally performed by a specialist or data scientist.
explainer.whyItMatters: It can reduce the manual effort needed for analysis by automating work normally done by specialists. This connects machine learning and language processing directly to business intelligence and analytics workflows.
misconceptions: It is not simply another name for business intelligence; it builds on business intelligence and analytics by adding automation.
It is not a separate name for machine learning or natural language processing; it employs both for analysis.
Automating analysis processes does not mean every task performed by a data scientist disappears.
